title: A study to learn about the safety and effects of IPN60330 in adults with advanced solid tumors
official: An open-label, phase I/II first-in-human, dose escalation, dose optimization, and expansion study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, immunogenicity, and antitumor activity of IPN60330 in adult participants with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors
summary:
Main objective: Phase Ia: To  evaluate  the  safety  and  tolerability  of IPN60330 and determine the MTD/MAD in participants with tumor type of interest. 
Phase Ib: To determine the optimal dosing regimen of IPN60330  in  participants  with  a  selected tumor type
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults ≥18 years of age
2. Histologically or cytologically confirmed locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor that relapsed or was refractory after being previously treated with standard of care therapy, or for which no available therapy exists
3. Have measurable disease per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1 and at least one measurable lesion not previously treated .
4. ECOG performance status 0–1
5. Life expectancy >3 months
6. Adequate organ function as per protocol-defined laboratory criteria
7. Willing and able to provide written informed consent by men and women as described by the study protocol
8. Agreement to comply with study requirements, including contraception measures
9. Tumour tissue is required at screening for biomarker analyses, including assessment of GPC3 expression. Eligibility for certain study cohorts may depend on biomarker status. Additional biopsies are required during treatment for selected participants across Phase 1a and Phase 1b
Exclusion criteria:
1. Second malignancy requiring active treatment within the past 2 years (with limited exceptions for curatively treated cancers)
2. Use of systemic immunosuppressive therapy including ≥10mgprednisone or equivalent. Corticosteroids for physiological replacement, contrast allergy prophylaxis and inhaled/topical administration are eligible
3. Receipt of live or attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks prior to study treatment
4. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
5. Known hypersensitivity to study drug or its components
6. Participation in another investigational therapeutic study within the required washout period
7. Any condition that, in the investigator’s judgment, would interfere with study participation or safety
8. Residual toxicities from prior anticancer therapy that are NCI CTCAE version 6.0 Grade ≥2 except for alopecia and stable chronic Grade 2 toxicities per investigator judgement
9. History of unacceptable Cytokine Release Syndrome and/or Immune Effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome
10. Prior exposure to a targeted therapy with a similar mechanism of action
11. Receipt of recent anticancer therapy without adequate washout period as defined in the protocol
12. Active or uncontrolled serious medical conditions (e.g., cardiovascular, pulmonary, neurological and gastrointestinal disorders)
13. Active or uncontrolled infections, including bacterial infections treatedwith systemic antibiotics within 7 days of study treatment and clinically significant viral infections. HIV and/or Hepatitis B are eligible providing there is adequate viral suppression as defined in the protocol.
14. Active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the past 2 years
15. Active brain or leptomeningeal metastases. Asymptomatic brain metastases or treated and stable brain metastases are eligible.
